Load in design, data:

Scaling the design to [0,1]:

scaled_design <- ScaleInputs(design[,1:4], parRanges, c(0,1))

We’ll create 2 objects to demonstrate emulation. Firstly, calculate the SVD and coefficients:

flow1_basis <- MakeDataBasis(flow1_data)
flow1_basis$grid <- data.frame(Time = seq(from=0,by = 0.01, len = 512))
flow1_coeffs <- GetEmData(scaled_design, flow1_basis, q = 5)

And alternatively, select a subset of timepoints:

time_inds <- c(50,150,300,500)
flow1_time <- data.frame(scaled_design, 
                         t50 = flow1_data[time_inds[1],],
                         t150 = flow1_data[time_inds[2],],
                         t300 = flow1_data[time_inds[3],],
                         t500 = flow1_data[time_inds[4],])

Splitting into train/validation for later:

set.seed(58219)
samp_inds <- sample(1:100, size = 100)
train_inds <- samp_inds[1:75]
val_inds <- samp_inds[76:100]

Default emulation

FitEmulators is the main function for training emulators.

If we just apply it to our data above, providing as little as possible:

em_time <- FitEmulators(flow1_time[train_inds,])
## The upper bounds of the range parameters are 108.4363 109.2586 108.7601 110.1666 834.0189 2111.214 1116.852 Inf 
## The initial values of range parameters are 2.168726 2.185171 2.175202 2.203332 16.68038 42.22428 22.33704 
## Start of the optimization  1  : 
## The number of iterations is  24 
##  The value of the  marginal posterior  function is  -23.75521 
##  Optimized range parameters are 3.750033 4.673904 8.141397 3.355738 21.71075 69.09918 15.16263 
##  Optimized nugget parameter is 1.601142e-05 
##  Convergence:  TRUE 
## The initial values of range parameters are 3.998621 4.028942 4.010562 4.062426 30.7547 77.85164 41.18425 
## Start of the optimization  2  : 
## The number of iterations is  28 
##  The value of the  marginal posterior  function is  -23.75521 
##  Optimized range parameters are 3.750033 4.673901 8.141389 3.355742 21.71072 69.09917 15.16263 
##  Optimized nugget parameter is 1.601148e-05 
##  Convergence:  TRUE
em_coeffs <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,])

Comparing what’s been fitted:

summary(em_time)
##            Length Class      Mode     
## em         1      rgasp      S4       
## method     1      -none-     character
## response   1      -none-     character
## mean_fn    0      -none-     NULL     
## train_data 8      data.frame list
em_time$response
## [1] "t500"
summary(em_coeffs)
##      Length Class  Mode
## [1,] 5      -none- list
## [2,] 5      -none- list
## [3,] 5      -none- list
## [4,] 5      -none- list
## [5,] 5      -none- list
unlist(lapply(1:5, function(k) em_coeffs[[k]]$response))
## [1] "C1" "C2" "C3" "C4" "C5"

This highlights a key difference in the default behaviour:

  • If the provided data includes a column named C1, FitEmulators will automatically set all preceding columns as the emulator inputs, and will train emulators for C1 and all subsequent columns. Here, flow1_coeffs containa the leading 5 coefficients, hence 5 emulators have been trained.

  • There’s no column named C1 in flow1_time. Given no other information, FitEmulators assumes the final column is the target output, and all preceding columns are inputs. Therefore, t50, t150 and t300 have been included as predictors (along with the 4 actual inputs) for emulating t500:

em_time$em
## 
## Call:
## RobustGaSP::rgasp(design = tData_input, response = tData_response, 
##     nugget.est = nugget, kernel_type = covariance)
## Mean parameters:  -2.791063 
## Variance parameter:  87.73041 
## Range parameters:  3.750033 4.673904 8.141397 3.355738 21.71075 69.09918 15.16263 
## Noise parameter:  0.001404689

To instead get what we obviously intend here (emulate each of the 4 time points using the 4 input columns), we need to add some extra information. First, we can point towards which columns are inputs:

em_time <- FitEmulators(flow1_time[train_inds,], input = 1:4)
summary(em_time)
##            Length Class      Mode     
## em         1      rgasp      S4       
## method     1      -none-     character
## response   1      -none-     character
## mean_fn    0      -none-     NULL     
## train_data 5      data.frame list
em_time$response
## [1] "t500"

This still fits a single emulator for t500, but now only uses the first 4 columns as inputs. To emulate all 4 outputs:

em_time <- FitEmulators(flow1_time[train_inds,], input = 1:4, output = c('t50', 't150', 't300', 't500'))
summary(em_time)
##      Length Class  Mode
## [1,] 5      -none- list
## [2,] 5      -none- list
## [3,] 5      -none- list
## [4,] 5      -none- list
unlist(lapply(1:4, function(k) em_time[[k]]$response))
## [1] "t50"  "t150" "t300" "t500"

(Alternatively, can select the outputs with column indices:)

em_time <- FitEmulators(flow1_time[train_inds,], input = 1:4, output_inds = 5:8)
summary(em_time)
##      Length Class  Mode
## [1,] 5      -none- list
## [2,] 5      -none- list
## [3,] 5      -none- list
## [4,] 5      -none- list
unlist(lapply(1:4, function(k) em_time[[k]]$response))
## [1] "t50"  "t150" "t300" "t500"

Plotting emulators

The two main things we might want to immediately consider are leave-one-outs and predictions on some out-of-sample set.

We can produce these for an individual emulator:

Validate(em_time[[1]], flow1_time[val_inds,])

LeaveOneOut(em_time[[1]])

Or for multiple (recommended to store as a named object, as it will return each plot in a list, but also immediately print all in a single plot):

val_time <- Validate(em_time, flow1_time[val_inds,])

summary(val_time)
##      Length Class Mode
## [1,] 11     gg    list
## [2,] 11     gg    list
## [3,] 11     gg    list
## [4,] 11     gg    list
loo_time <- LeaveOneOut(em_time)

There’s other plotting options, e.g., ordering by index instead:

val_time <- Validate(em_time, flow1_time[val_inds,], by_index = TRUE)

And/or by input:

val_time <- Validate(em_time, flow1_time[val_inds,], by_index = TRUE, by_input = TRUE)

This doesn’t automatically print all plots, but the by_input plots can be found via:

val_time[[1]]$input

Refitting a specific emulator

By default, the same assumptions are used (currently) for each emulator. These might not be suitable across all outputs. Above, the out-of-sample predictions for t150 aren’t ideal (outside 95% prediction intervals for 6 of the 25 points), so we may want to refit this with a different method.

We can replace the existing emulator with a version refitted with different assumptions via:

em_time <- RefitEmulator(em_time, 't150', method = 'het')

Instead of rgasp, we’re tried fitting using hetGP instead. Reproducing the validation plots from before, we see the 2nd has been switched with the new emulator:

val_time <- Validate(em_time, flow1_time[val_inds,], by_index = TRUE)

At least when considering the 25 validation points, this has improved predictions.

Fitting different emulator types

We could directly compare different methods for emulating the same output. We could use FitEmulators as follows to fit for 4 different methods:

# emC1_v1 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 1:4, output = 'C1')
# emC1_v2 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'het', input = 1:4, output = 'C1')
# # emC1_v3 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'gp', input = 1:4, output = 'C1')
# emC1_v4 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'dgp', input = 1:4, output = 'C1')

And can then combine these into a single list to enable us to use the plotting functions as before:

# emC1 <- list(emC1_v1, emC1_v2, emC1_v3, emC1_v4)
# val_C1 <- Validate(emC1, flow1_coeffs[val_inds,], by_index = TRUE)

Different input sets

We could instead use different sets of inputs (more useful if emulating different outputs where different active sets of inputs, but as an illustration just done for C1):

emC1_v1 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 4, output = 'C1')
emC1_v2 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 3:4, output = 'C1')
emC1_v3 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 2:4, output = 'C1')
emC1_v4 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 1:4, output = 'C1')
emC1 <- list(emC1_v1, emC1_v2, emC1_v3, emC1_v4)
val_C1 <- Validate(emC1, flow1_coeffs[val_inds,], by_index = TRUE)

Different covariance functions

emC1_v1 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 1:4, covariance = 'matern5_2', output = 'C1')
emC1_v2 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 1:4, covariance = 'matern3_2', output = 'C1')
emC1_v3 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 1:4, covariance = 'sexp', output = 'C1')
emC1 <- list(emC1_v1, emC1_v2, emC1_v3)
val_C1 <- Validate(emC1, flow1_coeffs[val_inds,], by_index = TRUE)

With/without nugget

Could also compare fitting the emulator with and without a nugget term:

emC1_v1 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 1:4, output = 'C1', nugget = TRUE)
emC1_v2 <- FitEmulators(flow1_coeffs[train_inds,], method = 'rgasp', input = 1:4, output = 'C1', nugget = FALSE)
emC1 <- list(emC1_v1, emC1_v2)
val_C1 <- Validate(emC1, flow1_coeffs[val_inds,], by_index = TRUE)
